title: Closed-support amplitude
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a
closed immersion, with open
complement $j$, and let $A$ be finite. Suppose that
direct image on the etale sites
satisfies $R^qj_*M=0$ for every module sheaf $M$ and every
$q>c$, where $c\geq0$. Then, in the
ordinary derived categories,

$$
Ri^!D^{[a,b]}(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)
\subseteq D^{[a,b+c+1]}(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A).
$$

If additionally every $R^qj_*F$ is
constructible for
constructible $F$, the same assertion holds with constructible
cohomology on both sides.

proof.text: Let P=j^*, G=j_*, I=i_* and E=Ri^!. Exact pullback preserves the interval [a,b], using Functor.homologyConcentratedIn_mapDerivedCategory_obj. In particular P(K) is bounded. All functors here act on the ordinary derived categories of ModuleCat-valued etale sheaves.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 1–2; finite truncation induction replaces the hypercohomology spectral sequence.

proof.text: R(G) is triangulated and commutes with shifts. Its value on a sheaf in degree zero is nonnegative by Functor.isGE_rightDerivedFunctor_obj_singleFunctor, obtained from the bounded-below/unbounded comparison; hcd bounds it above by c. Apply the proved source-library DerivedCategory.isGE_obj_of_isGE and isLE_obj_of_isLE (WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.TStructure) to P(K), with d=0 and d=c. These are finite inductions on truncation triangles, whose pure-degree terms are the corresponding cohomology sheaves shifted into their degrees. They give L=R(G)(P(K)) in [a,b+c]. No spectral sequence or abutment filtration is used.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 1–2; finite truncation induction replaces the hypercohomology spectral sequence.

proof.text: Take the distinguished closed-support triangle F -> K -> L -> F[1], with F=R(I)(E(K)). Its cohomology sequence gives H^(n-1)(L) -> H^n(F) -> H^n(K). For n<a both outer terms vanish. For n>b+c+1 the first vanishes because n-1>b+c and the second because n>b, using c>=0. ShortComplex.Exact.isZero_X2 therefore gives H^n(F)=0 outside [a,b+c+1].

proof.text: A closed immersion is finite, so I is exact on module-valued sheaves by the source finite-pushforward theorem. It is faithful by closed-pushforward full faithfulness. Functor.rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory identifies R(I) with its exact termwise derived functor. Functor.homologyConcentratedIn_of_homologyConcentratedIn_mapDerivedCategory_obj reflects the interval bound from F to E(K).

proof.text: For the constructibility clause convert the global finite-constant-value predicate to the source IsConstructibleSheaf predicate by isConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf_iff_isConstructibleSheaf. Both have the same finite global stratification convention over finite commutative A. The proved boundedConstructible.mapDerivedCategory_upperStar applies exact pullback and the constructible-pullback theorem to give bounded constructible P(K).

source.place: Proof paragraphs 1–2; finite truncation induction replaces the hypercohomology spectral sequence.

proof.text: Let CT be DerivedCategory.homologyProperty (constructibleSheaf (ModuleCat A) T). The finite-ring kernel, cokernel and extension instances make CT triangulated. Its inverse image under R(G) is triangulated as well. The extra hypothesis, converted through the comparison of predicates, puts every constructible sheaf in degree zero into this inverse image. The proved source-library DerivedCategory.prop_of_bounded (finite induction on truncation triangles) therefore yields CT(L). Applying CT.ext_of_isTriangulatedClosed1 to the closed-support triangle and the hypotheses CT(K), CT(L) yields CT(F). This replaces both the spectral-sequence-page argument and its finite abutment filtration.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 1–2; finite truncation induction replaces the hypercohomology spectral sequence.

proof.text: Functor.rightDerivedFunctorHomologyFunctorIso identifies H^q(F) with I(H^q(E(K))). Pull this constructible sheaf back by i^*. The isomorphism counit i^*I -> Id transports constructibility to H^q(E(K)); finally convert the source predicate back to IsConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf. Combine with the already proved interval bound, with no restriction on a<=b and no advance boundedness assumption on E(K).
